instruction: Use ${!var} for indirect variable reference

Use indexed arrays with compound assignment
output: files=(/etc/hostname /etc/resolv.conf /etc/hosts); for f in "${files[@]}"; do [ -r "$f" ] && cat "$f"; done

instruction: Use indexed arrays to store command output lines
output: mapfile -t pids < <(pgrep java); echo "Java PIDs: ${pids[*]}"; kill "${pids[@]}"

instruction: Use associative array as lookup table
Print all keys and values from an associative array
output: declare -A users=( [alice]=1001 [bob]=1002 ); for key in "${!users[@]}"; do echo "$key -> ${users[$key]}"; done

instruction: Use here-doc to pass stdin to a while loop

while read pkg ver; do echo "$pkg version $ver"; done << 'EOF'
nginx 1.24
mysql 8.0
python 3.11
EOF

Use readline bind to create a keyboard shortcut
Set readline to use case-insensitive tab completion

instruction: Use expect to handle password prompt interactively
output: expect -c 'spawn ssh user@host; expect "password:"; send "mypass\r"; interact'

instruction: Use expect with timeout and conditional branches
output: expect -c 'set timeout 10; spawn scp file user@host:/tmp/; expect { "password:" { send "mypass\r"; exp_continue } "100%" { puts "done" } timeout { puts "fail"; exit 1 } }'

instruction: Use expect to auto-answer yes/no prompts
output: expect -c 'spawn apt install -y somepackage; expect "Do you want to continue?"; send "y\r"; expect eof'
